Where would you recommend visiting? I'm planning for Japan to be this years annual vacation spot and I'd like to see a little bit of everything. That being said, I'd like to see the countryside and perhaps a few different temples. I was told I would enjoy Hokkaido.

Hokkaido is awesome any season but it's very skimpy on anything really Japanese ... It has some of the best snow and powder in the world and the snow festival is worth going to once.

I've heard it's like going to New Zealand or the Applachias in the U.S.

Susukino is a huge drinking party on the weekend. Susukino is almost in the heart of Sapporo.

There aren't many temples and shrines and you have to dig for them.

If you did Hokkaido:

  1. Jingu in Sapporo (main temple)
  2. The pioneer town exhibit on the outskirts of Sapporo
  3. An onsen (hot spring water bath) and be prepared to be naked with our her people
  4. Niseko for skiing
  5. Hakodate for its fresh seafood market and wharf
  6. Furano in early fall for a beautiful patchwork of fields and colors

I can recommend lots of activities based on the season for Hokkaido.

As for the Japanese experience go to Kyoto and hang out in Osaka. Those 2 cities will have everything besides Akihabara that Tokyo has to offer.

Roppongi in Tokyo is ... Not what you'd imagine and actually sucks.

Travel around Japan, expect all public transport to be on time. Winter and buses are the exception.

Japan is like New Zealand and England with islands but there is an over night train that connects Tokyo and Sapporo -- plane is faster. Japan is roughly the size of California but spread out from San Diego to about Seattle (more like San fransico if you take out Okinawa). You really don't need a rent-a-car and can doost things by train and taxi. Taxi drivers do like congested roads but even if you are passed out drunk they will still a congested road only. No laws like in Korea that fine taxi drivers for over charging you.

Depending on your time frame and money -- region only isn't so bad.

Even though I love Japan, I don't normally recommend the Geisha and Kyoto routine because the festivals are that much better and there's more to see than paying top dollar to drink with a MAIKO training to be a Geisha.

I'd really try to hit the yosakoi festival in Sapporo since it also has the Hokkaido shrine festival just a tad earlier in the month.

Now ... If you have kids I double down on hitting a festival and possibly throw in Tokyo Disneyland.

If you really are interested in the wilderness routine then Hokkaido and Sapporo would be a pretty good match!

I've worn out my youth and extended that as long as possible so if you didn't grow up listening to Rush singing Tom Sawyer you'll have a blast!

Tokyo and Osaka are pretty much English friendly to the point that you can't pick up any Japanese anymore :-( Sapporo and Hokkaido on the other hand is really spotty but the locales will bend over backwards to help.
